- Throughput target: sustained 600 concurrent users, average 2 requests/sec per user (peaks expected during market open).

High-level recommendation (TL;DR):
- Primary capacity: H100s (80GB) for the 70B model to meet P95 < 200ms with streaming and KV prefix caching.
- Fallback capacity: A100 (40GB) or 8x A10/A30s for cost-efficient batch-fallthrough on non-peak traffic.
- Reserved throughput: plan for ~45-55k tokens/sec sustained (roughly maps to ~1,200–1,500 concurrent inference pipelines with your 2 req/sec average and average 60 tokens per response). We'll break this down per time-window in the workbook.

Susan / Rafael — quick technical follow-up from our microbenchmarks: 

Bench summary (internal tests — sequence=512, sampling top-p 0.9, streaming enabled):
- H100 (80GB) single model shard: P95 ~ 160ms end-to-end with token streaming (batch=1, KV hits at 30%). Sustained at 600 concurrent streams we measured ~48k tokens/sec with headroom.
- A100 (40GB) single model shard: P95 ~ 250–300ms under same conditions; acceptable as fallback but not for primary SLO.
- A10/A30 (24–48GB variants): better cost-per-token but required heavier batching to approach throughput needs; adds latency and is not recommended for strict P95 < 200ms.

Sizing notes:
- For your sustained 600 concurrent users (2 req/sec avg), we estimate needing a pool equivalent to 4x H100 GPUs to meet the P95 target with redundancy (automatic failover + canary traffic). That maps to reserved throughput of ~50k tokens/sec.
- If you want N+1 redundancy and room for autoscale bursts, consider reserving 5 H100s or 4 H100s + 8 A100s as a blended option (primary low-latency capacity + cost-efficient burst capacity).

Caveats:
- These numbers assume our streaming runtime is running with KV prefix caching and a per-request pipeline that avoids extra decoder-side pre/post processing. If your prompt engineering increases average output length or includes heavy tool calls, we should re-run with your real prompt set.

I'll be available for the PoV; Rafael, let me know when to provision the H100 pool.

—Aditya
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

2) Cold-start/scale: what is the expected cold-start/additional latency when we scale from 4 -> 8 H100s (if autoscaling is triggered)? We prefer to keep the application-level P95 under 300ms during scaling events.

Available PoV windows: next Tue (22 Jun) or Thu (24 Jun) — afternoons PT. We can block a 2-hour slot for run-throughs and to push some synthetic peak traffic.

Susan — excellent questions. Quick answers and plan: 

1) Streaming + billing/reservation: Reserved throughput is measured in tokens/sec. Streaming token emission counts toward reserved tokens/sec. For PoV we'll provision a dedicated H100 pool with a reservation equal to the test-profile peak (we'll set it to 60k tokens/sec for the synthetic runs). We'll provide a short doc in the drive link about how tokens are calculated for billing.

2) Cold-start/scale latency: Our autoscaler provisions new H100 containers with optimized kernel warm-up; typical add-latency to reach steady-state is ~45–90s depending on model shard placement. During scale events we recommend a small buffer (N+1) in reserved capacity to keep P95 under 300ms — this is why we suggested either 5x H100 or blended 4x H100 + 8 A100s.

PoV scheduling: Tue, 22 Jun, 1:00–3:00 PM PT works for us. We'll provision the H100 pool and share test harness details by Monday end-of-day.

Deliverables before PoV:
- redwood-dedicated-sizing-v2.xlsx (attached) — detailed GPU mix and monthly cost bands.
- perf-results-summary.csv (attached) — microbenchmark results.
- Drive link with test harness and token calculation doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/finserv-perf

If you want, we can also include a short A/B run where we route ~20% of traffic to an A100 fallback to compare end-to-end latency and cost. Let me know.
